bullets.title: FOMC Decision Today: Market Pricing ~31% Hike Probability, Hold Expected
bullets.body: Markets head into today's FOMC decision with only ~24-31% probability of a 25bp hike priced in; consensus firmly expects hold but Citadel has publicly called for a hike. Goldman flags this would be the largest meeting-day 'surprise' in nearly 30 years. MOVE index has moved to Bullish TREND ahead of the meeting, signaling rising bond volatility. Fed Chair Warsh has long signaled aversion to forward guidance, and his hawkish lean is being watched closely.

bullets.title: Oil Surges 5-7% on Iran Strikes and Hormuz Disruption Fears; Airlines Pressured
bullets.body: WTI crude hit $83-85/bbl (+5-7%) as US strikes near Piranshahr in Iran's West Azerbaijan province escalated Middle East tensions, and the Houthi attack forced Saudi Aramco to shut its 400k b/d Jazan refinery. Brent futures rose to $88.13/bbl. Airlines are taking collateral damage with AAL -3.7%, DAL -2.6%, UAL -2.3% premarket. Iran denied seeking US negotiations and threatened unauthorized vessels with 'immediate action.'

bullets.title: S&P 500 +0.8% Despite Geopolitical Noise; VIX +7.9% to 19.65
bullets.body: US equities are shrugging off overnight Iran missile strikes and Korean market turmoil: S&P 500 at 7,370 (+0.8%), NDX +0.3%, with Equal-Weight S&P ($RSP) hitting all-time highs. VIX rose 7.9% to 19.65. Breadth was solid with 71% of S&P stocks up +2.6% avg yesterday, though gains were concentrated outside retail-owned momentum names.

bullets.title: KOSPI Crashes 6%, Down 39.7% from ATH; Historic Back-to-Back Circuit Breakers
bullets.body: South Korean stocks plunged 6% in the latest session, falling 39.7% from all-time highs and triggering back-to-back circuit breakers for the first time in KOSPI history. The proximate cause was SK Hynix's earnings miss. A 3x levered SK Hynix ETP (Ireland-listed) is down 96% since mid-June; a domestic single-stock leveraged ETF lost 80% in under two months as retail investors bought it on margin. South Korea's FSC is considering restricting single-stock levered ETFs to professional investors only.

bullets.title: Hedge Funds Execute Largest 3-Day Degrossing Since Nov 2022; Mag 7 Near 1-Year Lows
bullets.body: GS Prime Brokerage reports the Fri-Tue degrossing was the largest in 3+ years and the biggest for single names since March 2025. Global Info Tech saw its largest long-selling on record since 2016 over the past three sessions; memory stocks were net sold again with short selling resuming. Mag 7 positioning sits at 6th and 4th percentiles on net exposure and long/short ratio respectively. The de-grossing was primarily short-covering in macro products; levered ETF unwind is reportedly ~90% complete per JPM.

bullets.title: Momentum Factor Down 29% (96th Percentile Drawdown); Recovery Path Volatile
bullets.body: Price Momentum's rolling 3-month drawdown hit -29%, a 96th-percentile extreme. Goldman's high-beta momentum basket is on track for its worst monthly performance in history. SOXL fell 15% yesterday on 125M+ share volume. Historical non-recessionary precedent suggests the worst decline may be behind (median max drawdown was -26.5%), but sharp reversals to prior peaks are rare. Vol-control allocations have fallen from 96th to 76th percentile, and 1-month momentum volatility needs to drop below 90th percentile (~0.012) for stabilization.

bullets.title: AI Capex ROI Debate Intensifies; Hyperscaler CDS at Record Wides
bullets.body: Hyperscaler CDS spreads for Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have risen to record levels as markets price the risk of AI capex not generating commensurate returns. Goldman estimates ~$250B of hyperscaler debt issuance to finance 33% of 2026 AI capex, rising to 35% in 2027. Citi TMT notes HY credit reversed its AI recommendation from OW to UW after AI returned 8.5% through June but lagged by -300bp in July. Nvidia B200 GPU rental rates are up 9% from Q2 and 22% above Q1, indicating compute demand remains robust despite the credit market skepticism.

bullets.title: Big Tech Earnings Gauntlet Tonight: META, MSFT, ARM, QCOM in Focus
bullets.body: Tonight's slate — META, MSFT, ARM, QCOM — is the highest-stakes batch of the cycle. Street expects MSFT Azure +40-41% y/y and FY27 capex ~$250B; META 2Q revenue +28% y/y with 2026 capex at $134-155B and FY27 potentially >$200B. MS notes STX's record beat (SepQ EPS guide $7.30, +25% above consensus) and Teradyne's beat (+104% y/y memory revenue) as positive bellwethers. Per Citi, semis momentum positioning has declined 1000bps from 1500bps in June; software investors rotating back toward application names.

bullets.title: Semis: NDX Pacing Largest Monthly Outperformance Since 2002, But Breadth Reset
bullets.body: Despite the selloff in names like KLAC (-9.5% premarket) and VRT (-13%), NDX is pacing its largest monthly outperformance vs the S&P since 2002, and semis vs the S&P since September 2001. JPM notes that when SOX goes from 100% to 0% of members above the 50-day MA, average 1-year forward returns are ~50%. KLAC's near-term earnings were underwhelming but management is constructive on 2027 as WFE approaches $190B+.

bullets.title: Tech CDS Spreads Widening; Oracle and CoreWeave in a Separate (Worse) League
bullets.body: Per Torsten Slok data, CDS spreads for tech names broadly are widening, with Oracle and CoreWeave deteriorating at what analysts describe as 'alarming rates' relative to peers. NVIDIA's CDS spread surged to record levels this session, and MSFT short interest hit its highest level since May 2015.

bullets.title: SaaS Multiples Under Pressure; IGV -16.7% YTD, All-SaaS at 5.0x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's SaaS composite trades at 5.0x FY+2 EV/Sales, with multiples down 5.7% week-over-week. IGV is -16.7% YTD vs S&P 500 +8.9%. Enterprise SaaS faces a structural rethink: per-seat licensing is challenged by AI-native workflows, and the SaaSpocalypse erased $1T+ from enterprise software valuations. Citi notes software investors are reconsidering the application space as semis sentiment softens.

bullets.title: NextEra/Brookfield Announce $100B Kentucky Data Center Campus; ERCOT Baseload Surges
bullets.body: NextEra and Brookfield will build a $100B+ data center campus at a decommissioned Cold War uranium-enrichment facility in Paducah, Kentucky with 1.8 GW of capacity and 2 GW of co-located natural gas generation. Separately, ERCOT disclosed 65 GW eligible for baseload generation, well above the ~35 GW initial estimate. Morgan Stanley sees VST, CEG, and GEV as key beneficiaries of the structural power demand buildout for AI data centers.

bullets.title: Zuckerberg and Nvidia CEOs Push Back on Chinese AI Model Restrictions
bullets.body: Meta CEO Zuckerberg publicly argued the US should not block Chinese AI models to maintain competitive edge in the AI arms race, and also opposed broader regulations on open-source models. Nvidia's CEO defended open-weight AI models on the same day. The policy debate has direct implications for AI model competition and potential US regulatory risk for open-source infrastructure players.

bullets.title: Advantest Guides FY2027 Operating Income to ¥846B, 35% Above Prior Guidance
bullets.body: Advantest raised its full-year 2027 operating income guidance to ¥846B from ¥627.5B, beating Bloomberg consensus of ¥708.5B by ~19%. This is a meaningful read-across for semiconductor test equipment demand driven by AI/HBM ramps, consistent with Teradyne's record memory quarter (+104% y/y) and KLAC's advanced packaging revenue up 70% YoY.

bullets.title: JPMorgan Issues Broad Buy Signal on Stocks as Rotation Broadens
bullets.body: JPMorgan issued a buy signal on stocks, with the equal-weight S&P 500 hitting all-time highs and 71% of stocks up an average +2.6% the prior session. Healthcare and REITs are outperforming Tech and Momentum. However, one contrarian view argues the recent rotation is driven by short covering rather than genuine revaluation — positioning data supports this, given the record degrossing in tech longs.

bullets.title: Visa Q3 Clean Beat; US Payment Volume Growth +9% in July, Strongest Post-COVID
bullets.body: Visa reported Q3 EPS $3.32 vs $3.23 estimate, with +14% revenue growth to $11.6B and payment volumes crossing $4T. July US volume growth was +9%, the strongest post-COVID reading. Value-Added Services accelerated +34% y/y to $3.8B. FY26 revenue guidance raised. World Cup drove US cross-border volumes +25% y/y in June. 93% of sell-side analysts have Buy ratings, average target $413.78.

bullets.title: US Hotel RevPAR +6.3% YoY; NYC +35% on World Cup Final; Vegas -20%
bullets.body: JP Morgan lodging data for the week of 7/25 shows US RevPAR +6.3% YoY ($126), with luxury chain-scale up 17.2% and economy up 2.6%. NYC surged 35% on World Cup Final demand. Las Vegas was the worst performer at -20.4%. July is tracking +9.1% YoY, and the US has maintained above +5% RevPAR growth for 11 consecutive weeks. C-Corp operators (Hyatt, Marriott, Hilton) are outperforming consensus.

bullets.title: Physical AI / Robotics Entering Commercial Deployment; Nvidia Seen as Key Platform Play
bullets.body: Per Morgan Stanley and the All-In podcast, physical AI is achieving commercial ROI in industrial inspection, logistics, and manufacturing. Horizontal AI platforms like Nvidia (and Applied Intuition) are seen as likely to compound value across industries versus vertically integrated players. Boston Dynamics' Spot is the most widely deployed autonomous mobile robot; 1X expects limited consumer shipments in 2026. Defense applications growing; weaponized autonomous robots opposed by major players.

bullets.title: Energy Sector: Houthi/Iran Risk Driving Oil Spike; Saudi Aramco Rerouting Asia Cargoes
bullets.body: Saudi Aramco is considering a new pricing system for Asian-routed oil via Egypt as Houthi attacks disrupt Red Sea lanes, forcing Asian refiners to seek discounts for longer transit routes. The Jazan 400k b/d refinery shutdown and Ukraine's strike on a Rosneft refinery add to global refinery supply tightness. Energy equities are tracking oil's 5-7% rally; Canadian energy stocks (CVE +5.4%, OBE +5.5%) are broadly positive.

bullets.title: Bernstein Raises U.S. eCommerce Growth Forecast to 11% Q2; Amazon Focus Shifts to AWS
bullets.body: Bernstein upgraded its U.S. eCommerce growth estimate to 11% for Q2, up sharply from the recent 5-6% run-rate. Wayfair demand improved in May/June with growth above industry, and Morgan Stanley reiterates OW with $110 PT. For Amazon, the earnings outlook is more dependent on AWS AI tailwinds than retail eCommerce performance.
